title: What do the circled numbers in this grid add up to?
description: A grid of sixteen plus and minus numbers is played with the circle and strike game. Four numbers are circled, one from each row and each column, and added one at a time with every sign kept. Keeko's doubt that the circled numbers make nineteen, because the minus signs were dropped, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: circle one number in each row and column, then add the circled numbers one at a time, treating a minus number as a move down. Watch for the slip of dropping the minus signs and adding the digits.

source: The circle and strike game on a four by four grid: row 1 is 3, 4, 0, 9; row 2 is -2, -1, -5, 4; row 3 is 1, 2, -2, 7; row 4 is -7, -6, -10, -1
video_script.why: The child plays the circle and strike game on a grid of plus and minus numbers and adds the four circled numbers one at a time.
video_script.substitution: The book's own grid and the book's own circled numbers, negative one, nine, negative seven and negative two.
video_script.anchor: a four by four grid of plus and minus numbers from the book
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the circled numbers make nineteen, because one and nine and seven and two add up to nineteen. He dropped the minus signs, and negative one, negative seven and negative two move down, so the total is negative one.
video_script.payoff_line: Added one at a time with every sign kept, the four circled numbers make negative one.

final_answer.value: The four circled numbers add up to -1
final_answer.spoken: the four circled numbers add up to negative one

hold_back: The four circled numbers add up to -1
never_show: a second play of the game
maths_rules: game: circle a number, strike out its row and column, circle an unstruck number, repeat until none is left
plays: circle -1 (row 2, column 2), then 9 (row 1, column 4), then -7 (row 4, column 1), then -2 (row 3, column 3, the only one left)
a plus number moves up the number line and a minus number moves down
slip: dropping the minus signs gives 1 + 9 + 7 + 2 = 19
video_script.design: One four by four grid. Each circle is drawn and its row and column are struck out in turn, then the four circled numbers are added in three small steps on an upright number line, teal for moving up and amber for moving down.
open_questions: The book's answer says the sum is always negative one. This video shows only the book's play, and the next question tests other plays.
